items.target_of_objection: EXCEPT scope restatement 'rule proposal: ... Is fully exempt'
items.reviewer_position: The scope entry expressly names 'rule proposal' and states that it is fully exempt. This is textual content, not information available only in markup. The heading and its continuation together supply the exempted thing and exempting wording; excluding it merely because the continuation has no repeated subject misses the explicit exemption assertion.
items.reviewer_reply: The author's argument adds a same-sentence grammatical-subject requirement that section 4.2 rule 6 does not impose: the PART holds the exempted population or thing. The textual heading 'Scope of exemption for rule proposal:' identifies that thing, and its continuation 'Is fully exempt.' expressly states its exemption; using those exact spans does not invent words, and rule 8 permits discontinuous clause spans. The preceding Regulatory Fairness Act discussion supplies T4, as the author already accepts for R6. Section 10 is a coverage self-check, not permission to omit an otherwise recordable textual exemption; section 6's out-of-scope categories do not cover this legible heading and continuation.
items.author_position: 'Is fully exempt.' is a sentence with no subject and names nothing exempted from. 'rule proposal' occurs only as the object of 'for' inside the heading label 'Scope of exemption for rule proposal:', whose head is 'Scope'; it is not the subject of any exempting wording, so quoting it as the rule-6 PART would construct a sentence the text does not contain (spec section 1: record what the text says, no more). This differs from O2, where 'the proposal' is the subject within the same sentence as 'Is exempt' and the exempted-from thing is named in that sentence. Rule 6.3 does not fit either, since its case ('Small vendors are exempt.') has a stated subject. The fragment restates the scope of the exemption already recorded (R5 'This rule proposal, or portions of the proposal'; R6 'The entire proposed rule'; R9), and section 10 permits explaining it in out_of_scope_notes, which the revised note now does with the reason stated precisely.
items.effect: Proposed relation is NOT in the reference; it is recorded as contested and excluded from primary denominators. Any output unit asserting it is not scored against it.

cross_source_note: 26-19-039 author accepted an equivalent heading-style "Is fully exempt." statement as a relation (039 R4). The two isolated authors resolved the same construction differently; reported in FINAL as a reference-consistency limitation. Primary does not alter either reference.
